D: An uptight FBI agent and a foul-mouthed Boston detective team up to take down a drug lord.
P: Serve the mains at the Mullins family dinner.
S: Boston clam chowder with oyster crackers
Creamy clam chowder with bacon and potato, oyster crackers on the side

Creamy New England clam chowder with smoky bacon, potato and fresh clams, served in mugs with crisp oyster crackers and chives. Fry 3 diced rashers bacon until crisp, then add 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml fish stock and 300g diced potato and simmer 12 minutes. Add 1kg cleaned clams or vongole, cover and cook 4 minutes until open, then pick out the shells. Stir in 300ml thickened cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers and chives.
Crisp baked wings in hot sauce butter, blue cheese dip and celery

Oven-crisped chicken wings tossed in buttery buffalo hot sauce, served with a chunky blue cheese dip and cold celery sticks. Pat 1.2kg chicken wings dry and toss with 2 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt. Bake on a rack at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 100ml hot sauce and toss the wings through it. For the dip, mash 100g blue cheese with 150g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayonnaise and a squeeze of lemon. Serve with celery sticks.
M: Mullins family roast beef and gravy
Roast beef, crisp potatoes, honey carrots and pan gravy

Garlic and mustard crusted roast beef sliced pink, with crunchy roast potatoes, honey carrots and a rich pan gravy. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with 2 tbsp Dijon mustard, 2 crushed garlic cloves, oil and salt. Parboil 1.2kg quartered potatoes for 8 minutes, drain, rough up and toss in 3 tbsp oil. Roast the beef at 200C for 1 hour for medium rare with the potatoes on a separate tray. Add 4 halved carrots tossed in 1 tbsp honey for the last 35 minutes. Rest the beef 15 minutes. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, add 400ml beef stock and simmer to a gravy.
W: Sponge cake layered with vanilla custard and chocolate glaze

Two layers of light butter sponge filled with thick vanilla pastry cream and covered in a glossy dark chocolate glaze. Whisk 3 egg yolks, 60g caster sugar and 2 tbsp cornflour, then whisk in 300ml hot milk. Return to the pan and stir until thick, add 1 tsp vanilla and chill. Beat 125g butter and 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, then 200g self-raising flour and 120ml milk. Bake in a 20cm tin at 180C for 30 minutes and cool. Split in half and fill with the custard. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream and pour over the top.
K: Irish whiskey, lemon and egg white shaken foamy, bitters and cherry

Irish whiskey shaken hard with fresh lemon, sugar syrup and egg white until frothy, served over ice with a cherry and a dash of bitters. For each drink, add 60ml Irish whiskey, 30ml fresh lemon juice, 20ml sugar syrup and 1 egg white to a shaker or jar. Shake hard without ice for 15 seconds, then add ice and shake again for 15 seconds. Strain into a short glass over fresh ice. Top the foam with 2 dashes of aromatic bitters and drop in a cocktail cherry. Repeat for 4 drinks.

dishes.n: Boston clam chowder with oyster crackers
dishes.make_ahead: Make the chowder base through to the tender potato up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; add the clams and cream on the night

steps.text: Fry the bacon until crisp, then add the onion and celery and cook until soft.
Stir in the flour, then the fish stock and potato. Simmer until the potato is tender.
Add the clams, cover and cook until open, then pick out the empty shells.
Stir in the cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers and chives.

veg.n: Boston mushroom and corn chowder with crackers
veg.make_ahead: Make the chowder base through to the tender potato up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; add the corn and cream on the night

steps.text: Fry the torn oyster mushrooms in the butter with the smoked paprika until golden, then add the onion and celery and cook until soft.
Stir in the flour, then the vegetable stock, the kombu and the potato. Simmer until the potato is tender.
Cut the kernels from the corn cobs, add and simmer 4 minutes, then lift out the kombu.
Stir in the cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with the crackers and chopped chives.

dishes.make_ahead: Toss the wings in the baking powder and salt and leave them uncovered in the fridge up to 1 day ahead, and mash the dip up to 2 days ahead; bake on the night

steps.text: Pat the wings dry and toss with the baking powder and salt.
Bake on a rack at 220C, turning once, until crisp.
Mash the blue cheese with the sour cream, mayonnaise and a squeeze of lemon for the dip.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the wings through it. Serve with the dip and celery.

veg.make_ahead: Cut the cauliflower into florets and make the blue cheese dip up to 1 day ahead and keep both chilled. Coat, bake and toss on the night.

steps.text: Cut the cauliflower into large florets and toss with the olive oil, baking powder and salt.
Bake on a rack at 220C for 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Mash the blue cheese with the sour cream, mayonnaise and a squeeze of lemon for the dip.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the cauliflower through it. Serve with the dip and celery.

dishes.n: Mullins family roast beef and gravy
dishes.make_ahead: Rub the beef up to 1 day ahead and keep it in the fridge, and parboil the potatoes up to 1 day ahead; roast and make the gravy on the night

steps.text: Rub the beef with the mustard, garlic, a little oil and salt.
Parboil the potatoes, drain, rough up and toss in oil.
Roast the beef at 200C for medium rare, with the potatoes on a separate tray.
Toss the carrots in the honey and add for the last part of the roasting.
Rest the beef.
Whisk the flour into the pan juices, add the stock and simmer to a gravy.

veg.n: Mullins family nut roast and gravy
veg.make_ahead: Press the nut roast mix into the tin up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; roast on the night and add 10 minutes

steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and mushrooms in a little of the oil until soft and dry.
Chop the walnuts fine and mix with the mushrooms, lentils, breadcrumbs, eggs, cheddar, thyme and mustard. Press into a lined loaf tin.
Parboil the potatoes, drain, rough up and toss in the rest of the oil.
Roast the nut roast and the potatoes at 200C.
Toss the carrots in the honey and add for the last 25 minutes of roasting.
Rest the nut roast in the tin before turning out and slicing.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, add the stock and soy sauce and simmer to a gravy.

ingredients.item: eggs (3 yolks for the custard, 2 whole for the cake)

steps.text: Whisk the yolks, some of the sugar and the cornflour, then whisk in hot milk. Return to the pan and stir until thick. Add the vanilla.
Chill the custard.
Beat the butter and remaining sugar, add the whole eggs, then fold in the flour and milk.
Bake in a 20cm tin at 180C, then cool.
Split the cake and fill with custard.
Melt the chocolate with the cream and pour over the top.

dishes.make_ahead: Juice the lemons up to 1 day ahead and keep them in the fridge; shake with the egg white and ice to order

steps.text: Shake the whiskey, lemon juice, sugar syrup and egg white hard without ice in a jar or shaker. Repeat for each drink.
Add ice and shake again, then strain into short glasses over fresh ice.
Top the foam with a couple of dashes of bitters and drop in a cherry.

af.make_ahead: Brew and chill the tea up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; shake with the egg white and ice to order

steps.text: Brew the tea bags in the boiling water for 5 minutes, remove them and chill the tea.
Shake 60ml of the tea, a drop of vanilla, the lemon juice, sugar syrup and egg white hard without ice in a jar or shaker. Repeat for each drink.
Add ice and shake again, then strain into short glasses over fresh ice.
Dot the foam with a few drops of syrup from the cherry jar and drop in a cherry.
